ordered_diagnoses: Congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles

s1.syndrome_frame: Persistent vertical misalignment with elevation deficit
salient_findings: Elevation deficit of the right eye
Anomalous band in the right orbit
Right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion medial to the medial rectus muscle
key_facts: 52-year-old woman
History of long-standing diplopia
Persistent vertical misalignment
Orthotropic in primary position
Elevation deficit of the right eye
Previous MRI of the orbits revealed an anomalous band in the right orbit
Surgical excision of the anomalous band did not improve motility
MRI of the orbits with and without gadolinium showed normal globes and optic nerves
Right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion was noted medial to the medial rectus muscle

differentials: Congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles
per_call: Congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles

shortlist: Congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles

shortlist.label: Accessory extraocular muscle
shortlist.why_kept: MRI findings of a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion with signal-intensity characteristics identical to those of extraocular muscle

shortlist.label: Brown's syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: History of long-standing diplopia and elevation deficit of the right eye, consistent with a congenital or acquired restrictive strabismus

shortlist.label: Duane syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Persistent vertical misalignment and orthotropic in primary position, with a possible restrictive component

shortlist.label: Superior oblique muscle palsy
shortlist.why_kept: Elevation deficit of the right eye, which could be caused by a palsy of the superior oblique muscle

shortlist.label: Congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles
shortlist.why_kept: History of long-standing diplopia and previous findings of an anomalous band in the right orbit, which could be related to a congenital fibrosis

raw.rationale: The presence of a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion medial to the medial rectus muscle with signal-intensity characteristics identical to those of extraocular muscle, as seen on MRI, supports the diagnosis of an accessory extraocular muscle. This finding, combined with the patient's history of long-standing diplopia and elevation deficit of the right eye, suggests that the accessory muscle is interfering with normal eye movement.

rejected.label: Brown's syndrome
rejected.why: Brown's syndrome typically presents with limited elevation in adduction, which is not explicitly mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Duane syndrome
rejected.why: Duane syndrome is characterized by limited horizontal eye movement, which is not the primary issue in this case

rejected.label: Superior oblique muscle palsy
rejected.why: Superior oblique muscle palsy would typically cause vertical misalignment that worsens in certain gaze positions, but the patient is orthotropic in primary position

rejected.label: Congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles
rejected.why: Congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles typically presents with restrictive eye movements and ptosis, which are not mentioned in the case
